Text:
Ben Thanh Market offers an introduction to Saigon's trading life through its architecture, goods and everyday exchanges. At the southern entrance on Le Loi Street, the clock tower identifies the building and provides a useful reference before entering the aisles.

The market at its present location opened in 1914. Earlier Ben Thanh markets stood near the river landing. This move recalls the city's growth through waterborne trade. Inside, stalls offer handicrafts, souvenirs, food products and prepared dishes.

Observe the market in two layers: the recognisable exterior and clock tower, then the interior aisles linking food, dried goods, handicrafts and souvenirs. Moving between the building's overall form and the smaller details of its stalls makes the visit more informative than a photograph alone.

Direct exchanges between vendors and customers are another part of the experience. Notice how goods are presented and arranged, and how stalls differ. Choose food or gifts after asking about prices and ingredients and considering your needs; this guide does not replace questions at the counter.

Start by identifying your entrance, explore one group of stalls and visit a food area if desired. Confirm prices and portions before ordering, and keep aisles clear for both visitors and people working in the market.
